To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the DEDIPAC Knowledge Hub has been successful in bringing together a multidisciplinary network to provide a state-of-the-art overview of the current knowledge on individual and contextual factors that determine diet, physical activity, sedentary behaviour, and their interaction.

the determinants of dietary behaviour and physical activity in Europe are highly complex and are influenced by individual, interpersonal, social, environmental and policy factors, and that there is a need for a more integrated approach to understanding and addressing the determinants of nutrition, physical activity and related non-communicable chronic diseases.

the determinants of nutrition, physical activity and/or sedentary behaviour can be categorized in terms of individual, social, environmental and food system factors, and that the most important factors in each category are different across the life course.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the causes of the major non-communicable chronic diseases that affect the health of millions of European citizens and their families, as well as the economic burden on the healthcare systems.
the causes of the ‘causes of diseases’ and the development of effective interventions to tackle the major, non- communicable diseases of the 21st century.
the causes of the major non-communicable chronic diseases, such as cardiovascular disease, diabetes and cancer, and their consequences for health and health care.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
DEDIPAC has provided a strong foundation to further the field of behavioural nutrition and the physical activity sciences in Europe.

the DEDIPAC Knowledge Hub has provided the first comprehensive overview of the current state-of-the art and has provided a solid foundation for future research and action in the field of behavioural nutrition and health.

the DEDIPAC Knowledge Hub was a success and that it should now be further developed and expanded to become a European virtual research centre and knowledge hub for the determinants of nutrition and physical activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have provided a solid basis for furthering our understanding of the determinants of behavioural risk factors for non-communicable, lifestyle diseases, which is a prerequisite for the development of evidence-based policies for prevention.
DEDIPAC has provided the foundation for a new, more comprehensive, approach to understanding the causes of the main causes of non-communicable, chronic diseases.
DEDIPAC has been able to provide the first overview of the state of the science in the field of behavioural nutrition and the first toolbox for future research in the field.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a need for more and better data on the determinants of behavioural outcomes, as well as for more and better evaluation and monitoring of nutrition and physical activity policies.
we now have a much better understanding of what drives dietary and physical activity behaviours across the life course.
the DEDIPAC Knowledge Hub has made important contributions to the field of behavioural nutrition and has provided the foundation for further work in this area.
